review_notes: I read all of lines 1–48 of ConditionalMain.lean. The file has four theorems, and every proof is a one-line term. jointDickmanLaw_of_published applies jointDickmanLaw_of_rational_fixedScale to rationalFixedScaleLaw_of_published. increasingOrderLaw_of_published and decreasingOrderLaw_of_published each apply their own *_of_jointDickmanLaw lemma to jointDickmanLaw_of_published. main_results_of_published builds the conjunction from the three earlier theorems. The only repetition is passing the same eleven hypotheses (hMR … hBill) over and over. That is routine plumbing, not repeated mathematical reasoning. The section-level `variable`/`include` setup already handles it. Pulling the shared `jointDickmanLaw_of_published …` application into a helper would just be a thin wrapper around existing API, which the rubric explicitly excludes. No proof in this file does nontrivial mathematical work, so I found nothing that would justify a shared lemma.
